what: What is stopping us, in plain words. Hand-written because a machine cannot say who is waiting on whom. A blocker that clears is DELETED, not marked done.

blockers.what: The data pipeline is broken, not just behind
blockers.why: Our weekly job that refreshes the funding data has been failing since Saturday — it stops partway through, at the step that classifies what sector each company is in. The consequence is visible: we can name eight sectors where we could name eleven, and that count is a figure on our own home page. Nobody is being served the bad numbers, because a safety gate is refusing to publish them — which is the gate doing its job. But the pipeline itself needs a person.
blockers.ask: This one needs you. It sits alongside the container redeploy in AWAITING_APPROVAL, and they are related.

blockers.what: Two publishes, and neither is risky
blockers.why: Yesterday's corrections are live in the database and not yet in the copy the site falls back on, so the two disagree about 22 fund names and 51 eligibility rules. And the container that runs the weekly job has never once published a safety verdict in its life, so the check our automated builds read has been dark since the day it was built. Both are ordinary publishing steps we have deliberately not taken on our own.
blockers.ask: Read AWAITING_APPROVAL when you have half an hour. No money.

blockers.what: Nine of the companies we grade ourselves against won a fund that no longer exists
blockers.why: Part of the target we measure against is unreachable by definition, and it was quietly inflating one of our numbers rather than measuring the product. Found only because we stopped a dead scheme being recommended and watched what happened to the score. I want the true count before proposing anything.
